Hi Daniel + Samantha,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Per our discussion, here is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the evaluation: 

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: validate an LLM assistant for clinical triage and patient message drafting with strict refusal behavior on high-risk asks.
- Success metrics: safety (no hallucinated diagnoses), refusal precision on excluded categories, latency <= 200ms p95 for short prompts, and generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE-style proxy + human QC).
- Constraints: PHI handling (VPC/private deployment option likely), limited token budget per call, and requirement for audit logs and denial reasons.

Recommended immediate actions
1) Model candidates: run head-to-head on these variants — redwood-open-7b-quant (fast low-cost), redwood-med-13b-finetune (higher quality for clinical prompts), fallback to redwood-compat-xxl for complex cases. We'll provide config tradeoffs.
2) Eval harness: we shared a quick eval suite (link & attachment) with prompt sets covering allowed/forbidden categories + sensitive refusal tests. Please review.
3) Safety checks: we'll run guardrail prompts (explicit refusal templates) and a focused policy eval on sensitive domains (medical diagnosis, prescriptions, legal guidance). Expect an initial safety report within 72 hours after we get access to the sample prompts/data.
4) Data access: please share a redacted sample of representative patient messages (10-50 items) and any internal refusal examples; we'll run them through the harness.

Attachments (stubs)
- healthscope-prompt-sets-v1.csv (prompt set + expected behavior labels)
- eval-benchmarks-summary.pdf (current Redwood benchmarks & prior clinical evals)
- sample-patient-queries.zip (placeholder — please replace with redacted examples)

Open items / asks for you
- Send a redacted sample dataset (SFTP/Drive link fine).
- Confirm whether you want us to prioritize the private deployment path (VPC) for these evals or start in hosted sandbox (we can do both with limited data residency controls).
- Any compliance docs we should include in the pack (SOC2 evidence, DPIA)? Neha is looped for security-specific questions.

Next steps
- If you confirm data access and deployment preference today/tomorrow, we can schedule the eval run and deliver results by EOD Thursday (72-hr window).
- Rafael will propose an MA-outline and cost estimate for the Dedicated/Private path based on what you prioritize.

Thanks — I’ll watch for the sample data and preferred timeline.

Best,

Thanks Daniel — that plan works. Quick answers inline and a couple of technical notes.

Data share: 25 redacted messages is perfect for the initial run. When you upload, include a short note mapping columns (intent, expected_action, sensitivity_tag) — that speeds up the harness.

VPC vs hosted: agree with your preference for Private/VPC. Our recommendation: do an initial hosted sandbox pass (no PHI) to validate prompt/guardrail logic quickly, then replicate the winning config in the Private environment for a final safety pass. We’ll provide a checklist for the VPC provisioning (network ranges, KMS details).

Safety/guardrails: we’ll tune for conservative refusal. Implementation approach:
- Soft guardrail: instruction-level prompts that bias the model toward refusal for diagnostic/prescriptive asks.
- Hard guardrail: post-generation classifiers + exact-match policy lists to force denial for disallowed categories.
- Explanation policy: when refusing, the assistant returns a short refusal + suggested safe alternatives (e.g., "Please contact your provider" or "I can help draft a message to your clinician").

Initial eval plan (what we'll run after we get your sample)
- Behavioral tests: 150 synthetic prompts (sensitivity categories) + your 25 real examples.
- Metrics: refusal precision/recall, refusal calibration, quality proxies (BLEU/ROUGE for permitted drafting), latency and token cost.
- Regression checks: we’ll run against a baseline model you choose (recommend baseline = redwood-open-7b-quant) and flag any quality regressions if the primary candidate underperforms.

Deliverables (within 72 hours of data access)
- Initial safety report (summary + examples of failure modes)
- Prompt-set with suggested edits (CSV)
- Recommended model config + estimated monthly cost for Dedicated/Private path

Rafael and Neha — Rafael will draft the mutual action plan and ballpark pricing; Neha, can you confirm whether the SOC2 evidence bundle we have is sufficient for HealthScope or if they need a full DPIA?

Daniel — feel free to propose times for a 30-min follow-up at your convenience; I have open windows Wed 10:00-12:00 PT and Thu 14:00-16:00 PT.

Cheers,
Marissa
